data.description:
# Prep backlog is almost entirely producer-review flagged, starving the dispatcher's plan/intake fallback

## User story

As an operator, when the implement and audit budgets are exhausted, I want the dispatcher to have real plan/intake work to fall back to, so the local LLM slots are not left idle.

## Background

The host dispatch budget gates only `implement` and `audit`. `plan`, `intake` and `risk-effort` are deliberately uncapped, and since WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E / WL-0MWBT76WY00298AY a budget refusal is a continuable hold: the dispatcher records the refusal and steps on to the next ranked candidate, so a prep candidate behind a refused implement/audit can dispatch.

That fallback was supposed to keep the slots busy during the 2026-11-22/23 overnight run, but it had almost nothing to work with. Across the active roots, prep-stage supply at evaluation time (2026-11-23 10:15Z) was:

| Root | Prep-stage items (`idea`/`intake_complete`) | Admissible prep | Why not |
|---|---|---|---|
| ContextHub | 3 (`intake_complete`) | 0 | 2 x `needsProducerReview=true`; the third (WL-0MWRQYK3X007RQ1T) is a parent with 4 children and already has an outstanding `plan` dispatch marker at `intake_complete` |
| AI_Hell | 4 (`idea` + `intake_complete`) | 0 | all 4 `needsProducerReview=true` |
| SorraAgents | 1 (`intake_complete`) | 0 | `needsProducerReview=true` |
| Tableau-Card-Engine | 0 | 0 | no prep-stage items in the window |
| The Rising | 0 | 0 | no prep-stage items in the window |
| Game Curator | 0 | 0 | no prep-stage items in the window |

The leader therefore offered almost exclusively implement/audit candidates. Of 873 overnight refusals, 588 (67%) were `audit-budget-saturated`; the prep fallback could not fire because there was no admissible prep item to offer.

`plan_complete` items are implement candidates, not prep - a large `plan_complete` count does not help this fallback.

## Scope

1. Quantify prep-stage supply per active root: `idea` and `intake_complete` items, split by:
   - `needsProducerReview` (and the flag's provenance);
   - outstanding `plan`/`intake` dispatch marker at the current stage;
   - dependency/assignee/`startOn` hold;
   - attempt-budget or non-terminal-cooldown hold;
   - genuinely offerable.
2. For every producer-review-flagged prep item, establish provenance (which skill/phase set it: intake/plan question loop, audit reject, attempt-budget exhaustion, manual), age, and whether it has unresolved questions.
3. Write the root-cause statement for the empty prep bucket in the 2026-11-22/23 run, with counts.
4. Propose a remediation plan and create the follow-up work items:
   - clear stale `needsProducerReview` flags where there are no open questions;
   - batch producer interviews for items that genuinely need input;
   - change the skills so routine questions do not park items behind producer review;
   - seed new prep items where a root has none.
5. Verify the fix: for each active root, produce the `prep` bucket nominee in a live check-in (or an equivalent gate-classification read) and record it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A per-root table (ContextHub, AI_Hell, SorraAgents, Tableau-Card-Engine, The Rising, Game Curator) with the counts from Scope item 1, generated from `wl worklist --json` plus the gate predicates (not hand-sampled).
2. For every producer-review-flagged prep item: a row with `id`, title, flag provenance, flag age, and open-question status; grouped into "can clear now" vs "needs producer input".
3. A written root-cause statement for the empty prep bucket on 2026-11-22/23 with the evidence above (or corrected evidence if the investigation finds otherwise).
4. A remediation plan with concrete follow-up work items (each with an id, owner/queue and acceptance criteria) for stale-flag clearing, producer interview batching, skill changes and prep seeding.
5. Verification recorded: for each active root, the `prep` nominee from a live check-in (or the classification reason no nominee exists). Target: at least one admissible prep item on every active root, or a documented, justified exception.
6. Findings and follow-ups recorded on this work item; no dispatcher behaviour change in this item.

## Out of scope

- Changing the review-queue gate, the budget model, or the continuable-hold behaviour.
- Dispatching producer-review-flagged items without producer input.
- Implementing the remediation (separate items).

## Related

- WL-0MW9X7EJ6009EL6E - Host-budget refusal early-returns from head scans, starving plan/intake behind an implement candidate (completed).
- WL-0MWBT76WY00298AY - Implement continuable hold predicate and fix head-scan early returns (completed).
- Overnight evidence: `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log`, `<root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log*`, `<root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.

## Impact

When the implement/audit budgets are full, the dispatcher has real plan/intake work to fall back to instead of leaving local LLM capacity idle.


## Plan

Decomposed into seven child features (test-first), each a deliverable slice; the measurement slice is built before any investigation depends on it.

| # | Child | Role | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Test: prep-supply classification fixtures (WL-0MWTBJ5N1005BNXZ) | Pin the per-root prep-supply bucket semantics with fixtures before production code | — |
| 2 | Prep-supply report command (WL-0MWTBJ7G1004Y29B) | Read-only, repeatable per-root prep-supply read reusing the gate predicates | 1 |
| 3 | Per-root prep-supply table recorded (WL-0MWTBJ9AM003MLLL) | AC1 evidence: command output for all six roots, historical vs current | 2 |
| 4 | Producer-review provenance audit (WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI) | AC2 evidence: provenance, age and open-question status per flagged item | 2 |
| 5 | Root-cause statement for empty prep bucket (WL-0MWTBJCIV006BEGE) | AC3: counted cause(s) for the 2026-11-22/23 window, correcting evidence if needed | 3, 4 |
| 6 | Remediation plan and follow-up items (WL-0MWTBJEI2008UGUR) | AC4: four follow-up items with ids, owners/queues and ACs | 3, 4 |
| 7 | Verification and findings handoff (WL-0MWTBJGBS0085DG1) | AC5 + AC6: per-root nominee/exception, no-behaviour-change evidence | 2, 5, 6 |

Working assumptions (recorded in the Appendix comment):

- The read reuses `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` in `packages/herdr` (no predicate moves between packages), matching the read-only attribution pattern of WL-0MVR8FKMU009XTED / WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR.
- The intake snapshot is a point-in-time reading; a live read on 2026-11-23 already differs materially, so the root cause is evidenced from the run window, not from the current state.
- AC5's "at least one admissible prep item on every active root" is verified per root at verification time, with the follow-up item that closes each remaining gap named — remediation itself stays out of this item (Out of scope).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-23T13:50Z — plan session `herdr-1795440935-1077826-4881`: created seven child features, wired ten dependency edges, ran the six review stages and the AC-coverage review (100% of ACs covered by children), estimated effort Medium / risk Medium. No dispatcher, gate or skill changes.

## Evidence

- **AC1 — per-root prep-supply table (recorded, reproducible):** comment WL-C0MWTQO4WW006YDIC; methodology, command, `--now` and raw-JSON hash in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` → *Recorded prep-supply window (2026-11-23 10:15Z, WL-0MWTBJ9AM003MLLL)*. Child: WL-0MWTBJ9AM003MLLL.
- **AC2 — producer-review provenance audit (recorded, read-only):** comment WL-C0MWTTIOEN000M9LN — every flagged prep item's flag provenance, deciding evidence reference, flag age and open-question status, grouped *can clear now* (1) vs *needs producer input* (17); rule + recorded window in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` → *Producer-review provenance* / *Recorded producer-review provenance audit*. Child: WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI.
- **AC3 - root-cause statement (recorded):** comment WL-C0MWTUHK5H004OL7E and section *Root cause* below; full evidence, commands and per-root tables in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` -> *Root cause: the 2026-11-22/23 empty prep bucket (WL-0MWTBJCIV006BEGE)*. Child: WL-0MWTBJCIV006BEGE.

## Root cause

The run's prep bucket was empty at the **offer** layer, not the **supply** layer. Counts are evidenced in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` -> *Root cause: the 2026-11-22/23 empty prep bucket (WL-0MWTBJCIV006BEGE)* and in comment WL-C0MWTUHK5H004OL7E on this item; the full statement with commands is on child WL-0MWTBJCIV006BEGE.

1. **No prep supply - refuted.** 397 prep-stage items existed at `2026-11-23T10:15:00Z` and 123 were offerable by re-derivation (ContextHub 27/10, AI_Hell 78/13, SorraAgents 238/83, Tableau-Card-Engine 11/1, tce-the-rising 42/15, games_curator 1/1).
2. **The offer window was fully gated.** On the two roots that logged a gate classification every tick, 100% of the scanned candidate slots were gated (ContextHub 4,165/4,165: review-queue-hold 1,782 + audit-fresh 1,259 + producer-review 944 + code-freeze 88 + dispatched-marker 86 + 6 other; games_curator 768/768: producer-review 576 + audit-fresh 192). The dominant hold was the completed/in_review queue, not prep.
3. **The drain bucket was budget-capped.** 588 of 873 refusal decisions (67%) were `audit-budget-saturated`, 738 of them (84.5%) with both LLM slots free; the audit bucket that could drain the review queue was refused machine-wide.
4. **Producer review is real but minority.** 18 of 416 prep items were flagged (4.3%); 17 carry an unanswered producer question and the one clearable row is independently held by six unmet dependencies, so clearing could not dispatch it. That cannot explain an empty bucket while 123 prep items were offerable.
5. **Corrected intake evidence.** (a) The 873/588 figures come from `<root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log*` `kind=decision, operation=no-dispatch` entries, not from `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log` (1,029 reserve/confirm/sweep entries, zero refusals); (b) they are the recorded reading at `2026-11-23T10:12Z` and are no longer reproducible - the rolling 500-line logs have rotated, and re-running the intake command returns 0; (c) the "3/4/1/0/0/0 prep, 0 admissible" snapshot was a windowed reading that under-counted supply by ~10x on the large roots; (d) "almost entirely producer-review flagged" applies to the bounded scan window share (22.7% ContextHub / 75% games_curator), not to the 4.3% it represents of the prep backlog.

**Time dependence.** The window figures are historical and cannot be replayed (`wl` has no item-state history; `--now` freezes only time-derived gates). The current state differs: at `2026-11-23T22:32Z` the same read is 413 prep items / 128 offerable / 16 producer-review-held (the recorded 10:15Z read was 416 / 123 / 18; two ContextHub `ruff DTZ007` flags were cleared externally at `22:00Z` and one startOn matured). SorraAgents alone holds 238 prep items at the window clock (93 open, 145 blocked) versus the 1 in the intake snapshot.

**Open questions.** (i) A check-in records only `workItemId`, which mirrors `offers[0]` under v2; the per-entry `offers` payload is not persisted, so a prep nominee behind a non-prep head is not excluded by this evidence. (ii) There is no durable refusal log: the coordinator logs rotate within hours, so an overnight post-mortem cannot be re-derived - a durable refusal log (or longer retention) is a follow-up.


## Scope item 4 answer: remediation plan and follow-up items (WL-0MWTBJEI2008UGUR)

Four follow-up items, one per bucket, each linked back to this item and carrying the evidence rows. Planning only: no flag cleared, no skill edited, no dispatcher behaviour change.

| Bucket | Follow-up | Owner/queue | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4a stale-flag clearing | WL-0MWTVPJAN003GLAV | dispatcher maintainer / operator | Clears only the **1** `can-clear-now` row (`AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P`, dependency-held); the 17 `needs-producer-input` rows stay flagged. |
| 4b producer interview batching | WL-0MWTVPK65009NTER | producer | Batches the **17** `needs-producer-input` rows into one interview; each flag clears only when its question is answered. |
| 4c skill changes | WL-0MWTVPL1A005KB4D | skill maintenance (SorraAgents `skill/`) | **16 of 18** flagged rows are `question-loop`; routine questions must record an assumption instead of setting the hold. |
| 4d prep seeding | WL-0MWTVPM0D009FMG3 | dispatcher maintainer / operator | Guard: seed only a root with zero offerable prep; all six roots had >=1 offerable at 10:15Z (123/416), so this is a no-op unless a live read finds an empty root. |

**Dependency edges:** 4a and 4b depend on the provenance audit's `can-clear-now` / `needs-producer-input` groupings (WL-0MWTBJAV7002ZZQI); 4c and 4d have no blocking prerequisite. **Duplicate checks** are recorded on each follow-up (search terms + results; no scope duplicated).
data.title: Prep backlog is almost entirely producer-review flagged, starving the dispatcher's plan/intake fallback

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD (prep backlog starves the dispatcher's plan/intake fallback).

Test-first slice: pin the **per-root prep-supply classifier** bucket semantics with fixture-driven tests *before* any production code exists, so the measurement the rest of this item depends on cannot silently drift.

## Context

`classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts`) already returns a stable gate token for every refusal (`producer-review`, `assignee-hold`, `startOnNotReached`, `not-dispatchable`, `effort-cap`, …) — see WL-0MVR8FKMU009XTED. The prep-supply report adds only the dispatcher-side gates the classifier does not cover: an outstanding `plan`/`intake` dispatch marker at the current stage, attempt-budget exhaustion, and non-terminal cooldown. It must never re-implement the classifier's predicates.

## Acceptance criteria

- A new fixture-driven test module builds per-root windows from inline JSON (no live DB, no `wl` subprocess) and asserts the bucket for every case: offerable prep, `needsProducerReview=true`, outstanding dispatch marker at the current stage, non-empty `assignee`, future `startOn`, unmet dependency, attempt-budget exhaustion, non-terminal cooldown.
- Tests pin the bucket **precedence order** (producer-review → dispatch marker → hold → attempt/cooldown → offerable) with at least one fixture where several causes apply simultaneously, asserting the single reported primary cause.
- A negative case asserts a `plan_complete` item is never counted as prep supply, and that `completed`/`in_review`/`deleted` items never appear in any prep bucket.
- Tests assert **read-only** behaviour: no `wl` write is invoked, and the classified dispatch decisions are identical with and without the report module loaded.
- Tests assert the bucket names match the documented table in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (one source of truth; drift fails the suite).
- Changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply.test.ts` — new fixture-driven tests (does not exist yet)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `classifyItemForDispatchDetail`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` (asserted, never modified)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — `DowntimeItemInfo` fixture shape
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — canonical gate/bucket vocabulary

## Constraints

- No sleeps, no network, no live worklog; fixtures only.
- Must not modify gate behaviour — a failing assertion here is a finding for the parent item, not a licence to change predicates.

## Impact

The operator can rely on the prep-supply measurement: every prep item's bucket and single primary cause is pinned by fixtures, so a drift in the classifier-to-bucket mapping fails the suite instead of quietly changing the reported counts.
data.title: Test: prep-supply classification fixtures

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. Give the operator a **repeatable, read-only** per-root answer to "how much prep work could the dispatcher actually offer, and why not?" instead of a hand-classified sample.

## Context

The 2026-11-22/23 overnight run burned 873 refusals (588 `audit-budget-saturated`) with an empty prep bucket, and diagnosing it required classifying items by hand. `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` already attributes each refusal to a stable gate token; what is missing is a per-root, prep-tier-specific read that also applies the worker-side gates (dispatch marker, attempt budget, cooldown) and reports the genuinely offerable set.

Reuse, do not fork: `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (`downtime-worker.gates.ts`), `isAttemptBudgetExhausted`, the marker/hold predicates in `downtime-worker.selection.ts`, and the read-only attribution pattern established by WL-0MVR8FKMU009XTED / WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR.

## Acceptance criteria

- A read-only command/diagnostic emits **per-root JSON plus a human table** with counts per bucket: `offerable`, `producer-review`, `dispatch-marker`, `assignee-hold`, `dependency`, `startOn`, `attempt-budget`, `cooldown`, `other-gated` — and lists the offerable item ids.
- Inputs come from `wl worklist --json` where it already covers the item, plus a full per-root item read where the worklist has no prep subset; the gap and the fallback are documented in the command help and in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- The command accepts an explicit repeatable `--root <path>` (or reads the active-root set from config when omitted) and a `--now <iso>` frozen clock, so a past window can be replayed deterministically.
- Strictly read-only: no `wl` write, no marker/flag/assignee mutation. A regression test asserts the dispatcher's dispatched-item set is byte-identical with and without the report module.
- Output is stable and diffable — sorted by root, then bucket, then item id — so two runs can be compared in review.
- Bucket definitions and usage are documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, cross-referenced from `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD`.
- Changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.prep-supply.ts` — new report module (does not exist yet)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `classifyItemForDispatchDetail`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` (reused)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — marker/hold predicates (reused)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — item shape and gate-token types
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — only if a prep subset is added to `wl worklist --json`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — bucket table and usage

## Constraints

- No change to any dispatch decision, gate, cap or budget (parent AC6 / Out of scope).
- Do not move `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` into another package: reuse it in place, from herdr.


## Impact

When the implement and audit budgets are full, an operator can now see in one read-only command — per root and replayable at a past instant — how much plan/intake work the dispatcher could actually offer and the primary cause blocking everything else, instead of classifying items by hand.

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. Produce the **per-root prep-supply table** (parent AC1) as command output — not a hand sample — and reconcile it against the intake snapshot.

## Context

The intake table was assembled by hand at 2026-11-23 10:15Z. A live read on 2026-11-23 13:4xZ already disagrees materially (e.g. SorraAgents now shows ~93 open prep-stage items and AI_Hell ~22), so the "empty prep bucket" is a **point-in-time** finding that must be evidenced from the run window, not from today's state.

## Acceptance criteria

- A per-root table for ContextHub, AI_Hell, SorraAgents, Tableau-Card-Engine, The Rising and Game Curator is generated from `wl worklist --json` plus the gate predicates (not hand-sampled) — produced by running the prep-supply report across all six roots (paths: `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`, `SorraAgents`, `Tableau-Card-Engine`, `tce-the-rising`, `games_curator`), with the exact command line, `--now` timestamp and raw JSON reference recorded on `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD`.
- Bucket counts reconcile: the sum of buckets equals the count of prep-stage items in the window for every root, asserted by the command itself (no silent drops).
- The table records the historical-vs-current divergence explicitly: the 10:15Z snapshot from the description alongside the live read, with the re-derived window from the evidence logs wherever they disagree.
- Any row that had to be corrected carries an inline note saying why (a hand-edited count is not acceptable as the primary source — the primary source is command output).
- The table is reproducible: re-running the recorded command at the recorded `--now` yields the same table (modulo live data drift, which the timestamp pins).
- Recorded on `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD` as a comment and linked from its description.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — where the recorded table/methodology belongs
- `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log` — refusal evidence for the same window
- `<root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log*`, `<root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — per-root window evidence

## Dependencies

Depends on the prep-supply report command (child feature).

## Impact

Operators and the parent investigation can cite a reproducible, command-generated per-root prep-supply table - with the historical-vs-current divergence spelled out - instead of a hand-sampled window that under-counted prep supply by roughly an order of magnitude.

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. For every producer-review-flagged prep item, establish **where the flag came from, how long it has been set, and whether anything is actually waiting on the producer** — split into "can clear now" vs "needs producer input" (parent AC2).

## Context

The flag is the dispatcher's only persistent hold (`needsProducerReview === true` → `producer-review` gate). It can be set by the `intake`/`plan`/`interview` question loops, by an audit rejection, by attempt-budget exhaustion, or by hand. Nothing records provenance, so a stale flag is indistinguishable from a live question — which is what starved the fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

- A written **provenance rule** covering each flag source (intake/plan/interview question loop, audit reject, attempt-budget exhaustion, manual), naming the exact evidence fields it keys on (`auditResult`, last comment author/text, dispatch marker, timestamps) and its fail-closed behaviour when the evidence is ambiguous.
- For every producer-review-flagged prep item a row with `id`, title, flag provenance, flag age and open-question status; grouped into "can clear now" vs "needs producer input", recorded for every prep item with `needsProducerReview=true` on each active root with its deciding evidence reference (comment id / audit id / marker) and the flag age measured from that evidence's timestamp.
- Rows are grouped into **"can clear now"** (no open questions) and **"needs producer input"** (an unanswered question is recorded), with group counts per root and in total.
- Sanity check: the rule is applied to at least three items with documented history and its assignment matches that history (mismatch is recorded as an open question, not silently overridden).
- The audit is **read-only**: no flag is cleared, no item is reassigned (clearing is a separate follow-up).
- Findings recorded on `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD`.
- Changed-scope suite (`/skill:test`) passes if a provenance helper or rule test is added.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `producer-review` gate token (the predicate being explained)
- `docs/dev/rca-wrongful-needsproducerreview-removal.md` — history of the flag and its lifecycle
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — flag semantics and hold rules
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/{intake,plan,interview,audit,implement}/SKILL.md` — the call sites that set the flag

## Dependencies

Depends on the prep-supply report command (needs the classified item set as input).

## Impact

An operator can now see, for every producer-review-flagged prep item, what put the flag there, how stale it is and whether a real producer question is waiting — so stale flags can be cleared from evidence instead of guesswork.
data.title: Producer-review provenance audit

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. Write the **root-cause statement** for the empty prep bucket in the 2026-11-22/23 run — or correct the intake evidence if the measurement disagrees (parent AC3).

## Context

The intake hypothesis is: prep supply existed but was almost entirely `needsProducerReview`-held, so the leader had nothing to offer behind a refused implement/audit head. A live read on 2026-11-23 already contradicts the "no supply" reading for several roots, so the statement must separate *supply*, *gating*, and *time dependence* explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria

- A written root-cause statement for the empty prep bucket on 2026-11-22/23 with the evidence above (or corrected evidence if the investigation finds otherwise): the statement names the cause(s) with counts for the window and explicitly distinguishes **no prep supply** from **prep supply held by gates**, per root.
- Every number is traceable to evidence with the command used: `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log` refusal counts (873 refusals / 588 = 67% `audit-budget-saturated`), the per-root coordination/dispatch logs, and the prep-supply table.
- Where re-derivation disagrees with the intake table, the statement says so explicitly ("corrected evidence: was X, now Y, because Z") rather than silently rewriting it.
- The statement separates the historical window from the current state and labels which findings are time-dependent (e.g. "SorraAgents has ~93 open prep items today, 1 at 10:15Z").
- Every claim is traceable to a row/count in the prep-supply or provenance findings; unsupported claims are removed or marked OPEN QUESTION.
- Recorded on `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD` as the "Root cause" section.

## Key Files

- `~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.log` (+ `.1` rotation) — refusal evidence
- `<root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log*` — per-root check-in/offer evidence
- `<root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — per-root dispatch history
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — tier/bucket and gate semantics the analysis reasons about

## Dependencies

Depends on the per-root prep-supply table and the producer-review provenance audit.

## Impact

An operator reading the overnight logs can now see that the prep bucket was empty because the scanned candidate window was fully gated - not because there was no prep work - and knows which evidence must be retained to prove it next time.
data.title: Root-cause statement for empty prep bucket

## Goal

Parent: WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD. Turn the findings into a **remediation plan with concrete follow-up work items** (parent AC4) — planning only: no flags are cleared, no skill is edited and no dispatcher behaviour changes in that parent item.

## Acceptance criteria

- A remediation plan with concrete follow-up work items (each with an id, owner/queue and acceptance criteria) for stale-flag clearing, producer interview batching, skill changes and prep seeding — four items, each linked back to `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD` with the evidence rows that justify it.
  - (a) clear stale `needsProducerReview` flags where no open question exists;
  - (b) batch producer interviews for the items that genuinely need producer input;
  - (c) change the `intake`/`plan`/`interview` skills so routine questions do not park items behind producer review;
  - (d) seed new prep items on roots that have none.
- Each follow-up names the evidence rows (from the prep-supply table / provenance audit / root-cause statement) that justify it, and links back to `WL-0MWTAD1KM0081UUD`.
- Dependency edges are wired: stale-flag clearing depends on the provenance audit's "can clear now" grouping; interview batching depends on the "needs producer input" grouping; the skill-change and prep-seeding items have no blocking prerequisite.
- Duplicate check recorded: each proposed follow-up is checked against existing open/completed work with `wl search`/`wl list` and the search terms plus results are noted (no new item duplicating existing scope).
- The four buckets above are covered: stale-flag clearing, producer interview batching, skill changes, prep seeding — one item each, no bucket merged or dropped.
- Remediation stays **planned only** in this item: no flag cleared, no skill file edited, and no dispatcher behaviour change (verified by an unchanged dispatched-item set).
